name: Zoning and Permitting Framework for ADUs in Los Angeles County
headline: Zoning and Permitting Framework for ADUs in Los Angeles County
articleBody: Los Angeles County implements California’s statewide ADU statutes through local zoning and permitting procedures administered by Los Angeles County Planning. County guidance explains that ADUs are permitted on lots with existing residential uses, including single-family and certain multifamily properties, subject to development standards such as maximum size, height, setbacks, and lot coverage. The County’s ADU page notes that ADUs can be either detached or attached, or created by converting existing space, and that they are treated as accessory to the primary dwelling rather than separate primary units. Under California law as summarized in statewide ADU guides for 2025, homeowners are generally allowed **one full ADU per lot** and may also be able to add **one Junior ADU (JADU)**, subject to local zoning, provided both units meet setback, height, and building code requirements. State guidance requires that local governments provide “by-right” approval for ADUs that conform to objective standards and prohibits excessive parking or minimum lot size requirements that would undermine ADU feasibility. Industry explainers covering the Los Angeles region note that cities and counties may add their own **design, size, or parking standards**, but these must remain consistent with the state’s minimum protections for ADU development. Los Angeles County Planning has also adopted a **pre-approved plan program**, where professional architects’ ADU plans are pre-checked by Planning and Public Works. Project sponsors who use such plans can streamline parts of the review process because structural and code compliance aspects of the design have already been evaluated. However, applicants still need site-specific approvals, including zoning clearance, building permits, and any required grading, sewer, or utility permits, depending on site conditions.
